title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-04-ryan
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for quantization + prompt eval runs on Llama2-13b variants.

Notes to self / context:
- goal: understand quality delta (chat/QA) between fp16 baseline and q4_0/q8_0 variants when served with continuous batching + xformers kernels. want <3% relative drop on answer F1 while saving >2x token cost.
- baseline model: llama2-13b-chat FP16 (serving-runtime v0.9.4). eval harness: eval-run-2026-03-04-ryan-01
- quant candidates: q4_0, q4_1, q8_0 (hf-quant builds), plus experimental hybrid-int8 (local patch).

Quick results (rough):
- fp16 baseline (64-token avg): latency 110ms/token p95, cost unit 1.0, F1 (QA set) 0.82
- q4_0: latency 95ms/token p95, cost 0.48, F1 0.79 (drop 3.7%) -> promising but some hallucination on long context
- q4_1: latency 98ms/token p95, cost 0.52, F1 0.805 -> tradeoff looks better
- q8_0: latency 92ms/token p95, cost 0.42, F1 0.78 -> smaller model artifacts on math prompts
- hybrid-int8 (local): latency 85ms, cost 0.36, F1 0.80 but reliability flaky (kv cache mismatch on long seqs)

Prompt sets used (short):
- qa-short: 2k examples, closed-book QA, factual wiki-style
- qa-long: 600 examples, multi-paragraph context + questions (sensitive to kv cache)
- summarization-light: 800 docs (news blurb) -> eval Rouge-L
- instruction-chat: 1.2k instruction-following prompts (LLM eval rubric)

Observations / debug: 
- q4_0 shows token-level drift on numeric tokens (dates, small ints) -> inspect quantization table for embedding/kernel alignment.
- kernel selection: AVX vs xformers gives ~10% perf diff; try kernel=auto-routing in runtime config to pick best per model-length.
- reproducer: minimal repro for q4_0 hallucination in qa-long attached as eval-run-2026-03-04-ryan-01/id-7 (see linked github gist later).

To-do / next steps (priority):
- [ ] run more seeds (n=3) for q4_1 and hybrid-int8 on qa-long (JIRA-INF-842) -> schedule overnight on dedicated pool
- [ ] add prompt-level diagnostics: token-level logprobs + top-k mismatch for failing examples
- [ ] open tiny PR to serving-runtime to add fallback to fp16 when kv-cache-diff > threshold (link to PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412)
- [ ] run end-to-end latency/cost sim with batching=auto and cache hit-rate=0.6 (estimate cost savings)
- [ ] sync with Maya next Tue (she has new eval harness for multi-ref QA)

Open questions / experiments to try: 
- try mixed quant->fp16 hybrid for attention weights only (cheap to implement?)
- how much does prompt-engineering reduce the F1 gap vs switching quant profiles? Maybe 1-2% improvement with minimal prompt changes.
- check if instruction-chat errors correlate with tokenization edge cases (weird unicode)

Scratch notes: 
- quick CLI: ./eval_harness --model llama2-13b-q4_1 --prompts qa-long --out results/q4_1-qa-long.json --seed 42
- eval-run ids: eval-run-2026-03-04-ryan-01 (baseline fp16), eval-run-2026-03-04-ryan-02 (q4_0), eval-run-2026-03-04-ryan-03 (q4_1)
- rough budget estimate: if q4_1 stable, projected 2.1x cost savings vs FP16 at current traffic (contact finance if we commit Dedicated).

Random notes to self: 
- check conda env versions (pytorch 2.1 vs 2.2 behavior difference?).
- remind Asha to push kernel perf logs to S3 bucket (s3://redwood-perf/quant-2026-03).

End of scratchpad (save this, will prune into Confluence later).
